description: rnews_main.rs lines 210-226: the HLC clock is built in a block and bound to 'let hlc = { ... }', then immediately rebound as 'let mut hlc = hlc;' on the next line. The reader must track two bindings to understand that the result is mutable. This can be collapsed to 'let mut hlc = { ... }' in a single declaration. The comment '// The HLC is owned locally...' above the rebind is compensation for the confusion, not justification for the pattern.
title: let hlc = {...}; let mut hlc = hlc; double-bind is unnecessary
